A1.justification: Both 11-page PDFs describe the same DiffusionGS work, with readable text, equations, figures and tables supporting full comparison. Both end with references; neither supplied PDF contains appendices.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original object-generation and scene-reconstruction experiments, a user study, and component ablations in Tables 1–2.

after.justification: Section 4 retains the original benchmark results, user study and ablations reported in v3.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains identical Gaussian-predicting diffusion, scene-object mixed training, RPPC camera conditioning, dual decoders, losses and inference procedures.

E1.justification: Both retain Objaverse/MVImgNet object training, RealEstate10K/DL3DV10K scene training, ABO/GSO/RealEstate10K evaluations, and the same real-camera and text-generated examples.

E2.justification: Comparator membership matches throughout Table 1 and Figures 6–8, including the object-generation baselines, scene-reconstruction baselines and PhotoNVS comparison.

E3.justification: Both specify identical preprocessing, training budgets, resolutions and evaluation metrics. The one-input/ten-test-view evaluation and 25-person study of 14 objects are unchanged.

E4.justification: Table 2 retains the same component ablation. Section 4.2 and Figures 8–9 retain identical mixed-training, RPPC and generation-diversity analyses.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is identical: neither provides repeated-run uncertainty estimates or significance tests. Both retain the same random-seed variation discussion for generation diversity.

E6.justification: All numerical results and qualitative examples match. For example, Table 1 reports identical DiffusionGS PSNR/FID values of 25.89/9.03 on ABO and 21.63/15.87 on RealEstate10K.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(13), including the RPPC definition, camera-angle constraints and training objective, are identical. No mathematical assumption, derivation or formal result changes.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain identical claims about single-stage generation, view consistency, mixed training, RPPC, benchmark advantages and approximately six-second inference.

C2.justification: Explanations of geometry, view consistency, mixed-training benefits and comparator failure modes are unchanged. No applicability boundary or limitation is added or revised.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hyperparameters, GPU resources, data processing and the project-page link are identical. The added arXiv stamp hyperlink supplies no new implementation or code/data access information.

R1.justification: Section 2, research positioning and all 91 references are unchanged; no cited work or novelty relationship is added or removed.

P1.justification: The first-page arXiv stamp changes from v3 dated 8 March 2025 to v4 dated 26 June 2025. All paper prose, headings and document structure are identical.

P2.justification: Only the first-page margin stamp changes in appearance and placement. Figures 1–9, Tables 1–2 and their layouts are identical; rendered pages 2–11 match pixel-for-pixel.

improvement.justification: The methods, results, analyses, explanations and reproducibility information are identical across the supplied PDFs. The bibliographic stamp and hyperlink updates do not meaningfully affect the paper's clarity, evidential strength or overall quality.
